intro: Fundraisers persuade, negotiate and build relationships, the same skills that lead to marketing and PR leadership. The closest of the 25 careers below is Fundraising Managers, with a 95% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $125,470, which is 73% more than the $72,550 fundraisers earn.
why_it_works: Raising money means researching donors, telling a compelling story and asking for large gifts with confidence. O*NET rates persuasion at 4 out of 5 for this job, negotiation at 3.88 and coordination at 3.75. Public relations, advertising and sales leadership use the same skills, and 9 of the top 10 matches pay more. The gaps are time management and leading people.
tips: Fundraising management is the natural next step: lead a team and own a campaign target.
Public Relations Managers earn $146,910, which is 102% more, and are a 93% match.
Sales Managers earn $148,270, or 104% more, and value donor relationship skills.

faq.q: What jobs can former fundraisers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Fundraising Managers (95%), Public Relations Specialists (93%) and Public Relations Managers (93%), based on O*NET 31.0. Advertising and Promotions Managers are 92% matched and earn $133,660, which is 84% more than the $72,550 fundraiser median.

faq.q: Which careers for fundraisers pay more?
faq.a: 18 of the 25 matches pay more. Chief Executives earn $213,990 (195% more), Marketing Managers $166,790 (130% more) and Financial Managers $166,570 (130% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Executive roles usually need a graduate degree or years of leadership.

faq.q: Do fundraisers need another degree to switch?
faq.a: Usually not. 22 of the 25 matches need no more education than fundraisers already have, including all of the top 10, while 3 need a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 66% of workers in the closest match.

The skills that most often need work are time management, operations analysis, managing materials and managing people. Social perceptiveness already rates 3.62 out of 5 for fundraisers in O*NET, so running teams and campaigns is the main step toward management roles.
